## Abstract

Vision foundation models (FM) pretrained with self-supervised learning have become a powerful paradigm for transferable visual representations. 
However, extending strong 2D FMs to volumetric clinical modalities such as CT and MRI remains difficult because 3D architectures are computationally expensive and annotated 3D data are scarce.

This thesis studies how pretrained 2D FMs can be leveraged for medical image analysis in two complementary ways. 
First, we benchmark state-of-the-art 2D FMs on CXR and related radiological domains, comparing domain-specific models (RAD-DINO, Ark+) with general-purpose backbones (DINOv2) under frozen-feature evaluation, fine-tuning, and zero-shot transfer. 
The results show a clear generalization–specialization trade-off: domain-specific models perform best on in-distribution CXR tasks under frozen features, whereas general-purpose models retain greater adaptation headroom on out-of-distribution targets such as spine radiographs and mammography.

Second, we propose MedSliM (Medical Slice-level representation learning with Mamba), a self-supervised framework for 3D knee MRI that adapts the COBRA architecture to volumetric imaging. MedSliM encodes 2D slices with pretrained FMs and aggregates the resulting features using a Mamba-2 sequence encoder and ABMI. 
On MRNet, it achieves an AUROC of 0.936 for abnormality detection, outperforming the volumetric self-supervised baseline 3DINO with 0.922, and also generalizes to the unseen kneeMRI dataset. Overall, the results show that operating in the feature space of pretrained 2D FMs, rather than directly on raw voxels, provides a computationally and label-efficient route toward 3D medical image representation learning, while highlighting open challenges in interpretability, cross-plane alignment, and broader anatomical generalization.
 

## Data

1. [MRNet](https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/)
2. [kneeMRI](https://zenodo.org/records/14789903)
3. [fastMRI](https://fastmri.med.nyu.edu/)
